scenarios.description: A single missed Monday is forgiven; the rest of the week is kept.
scenarios.reasoning: R4 forgives the Monday miss because no day was forgiven yet that week and the count was 0, so the streak grows through it and forgive-1 fires. R3 then counts each kept day, reaching streak 5 on Friday, which fires milestone-5 per R7. At the Sunday week-end update R5 moves the count from 0 to 1 because the week had a forgiven day and no break.

scenarios.description: Six kept days, then a missed Sunday that is forgiven at the week's end.
scenarios.reasoning: The Sunday miss is forgiven under R4 (first miss of the week, count 0), so R3 counts it and the streak reaches 7, firing forgive-1. Friday's kept day hit streak 5 and fired milestone-5 per R7. The Sunday week-end update then applies R5, raising the count to 1 for the coming week.

scenarios.description: A miss at Sunday 23:59 and another at Monday 00:00 fall in different weeks, so each is forgiven separately.
scenarios.reasoning: R2 puts the Sunday miss in week 1 and the Monday miss in week 2, so R4 forgives each independently: forgive-1 on Sunday (count was 0) and forgive-2 on Monday (count was 1 after week 1's week-end update). The streak counts both forgiven days and keeps growing, hitting milestone-5 on Thursday. Each Sunday's week-end update raises the count, ending at 2.

scenarios.description: A forgiven Monday miss followed by a second miss on Thursday breaks the streak.
scenarios.reasoning: Monday's miss is forgiven (forgive-1) but Thursday's miss fails R4a because a day was already forgiven that week, so R3 resets the streak to 0 and R5 zeroes the count immediately, firing streak-broken. Friday's kept day restarts the streak at 1. The Sunday week-end update keeps the count at 0 because the week had a break, and no week-end letter fires.

scenarios.description: Three straight weeks each forgive one Monday miss; the fourth week's miss breaks the streak, and forgiveness works again the week after.
scenarios.reasoning: Each of the first three Mondays is forgiven, firing forgive-1, forgive-2, then forgive-3-limit co-firing with milestone-15 on the third Monday; each Sunday's week-end update raises the count 0 to 1 to 2 to 3, and the third Sunday fires forgive-off-warning. The fourth Monday's miss fails R4b because the count is 3, so it breaks: streak-broken-after-limit fires, the streak resets to 0, and the count drops to 0 immediately. The next week's Monday miss is forgiven again (forgive-1) because the count is back under 3, and no forgive-restored ever fires since week 4 contained a break. Under R4c, forgiveness stays off for the rest of the break week (26 Oct–1 Nov) and returns on Monday 2 Nov, where the miss is forgiven with forgive-1.

scenarios.description: After three forgiveness weeks hit the limit, a fully clean week restores forgiveness and the next miss is forgiven again.
scenarios.reasoning: Weeks 1-3 each forgive a Monday miss and the count climbs to 3, with forgive-off-warning firing on the third Sunday. Week 4 has no miss and no break, so its Sunday week-end update resets the count to 0 and fires forgive-restored. Week 5's Wednesday miss is therefore forgiven (forgive-1), proving the limit only blocks while the count sits at 3.

scenarios.description: The Sunday ending the third forgiveness week is itself the forgiven day and lands on streak 15, so three letters co-fire.
scenarios.reasoning: Week 1 forgives its Sunday miss (forgive-1) and week 2 its Monday miss (forgive-2), with the count reaching 2. Week 3 keeps six days, so the Sunday miss lands on streak 15: it is forgiven because the count was 2, firing forgive-3-limit, and R7 fires milestone-15 on the same day. The Sunday week-end update then raises the count to 3, which fires forgive-off-warning, giving the required order forgive, milestone, week-end letter.

scenarios.description: A week containing the US fall-back transition (2026-11-01); the 25-hour Sunday is still one local day.
scenarios.reasoning: R1 evaluates each local calendar date once, so the repeated 1am-2am hour on 2026-11-01 does not create an extra day: Sunday is a single kept day and the streak reaches 7. Saturday's miss is forgiven (forgive-1) under R4, and the Sunday week-end update moves the count to 1.

scenarios.description: A week containing the US spring-forward transition (2027-03-14); the 23-hour Sunday is still one local day.
scenarios.reasoning: The skipped 2am-3am hour on 2027-03-14 does not remove the local date, so R1 still evaluates Sunday once as a kept day and the streak reaches 7 with no letters. The week-end update leaves the count at 0 because there was no forgiven day.

scenarios.description: The user moves from New York to Los Angeles mid-week; each day is evaluated in its own recorded timezone.
scenarios.reasoning: R2 keeps every day in the Monday-Sunday week of its own local date, so the timezone change does not shift any day into a different week. Tuesday's New York miss is forgiven (forgive-1), the streak counts it, and Friday's Los Angeles day hits streak 5, firing milestone-5. The Sunday week-end update raises the count to 1.

scenarios.description: The user moves from Tokyo to London mid-week; each day is evaluated in its own recorded timezone.
scenarios.reasoning: Per R2 each day's local date decides its week, so Wednesday's London date stays in the same Monday-Sunday week as the Tokyo days. Thursday's London miss is forgiven (forgive-1), the streak reaches 7, and the Sunday week-end update moves the count to 1.

scenarios.description: Flying Tokyo → Honolulu crosses the date line eastward and repeats local Tuesday; the two Tuesday recordings collapse into one evaluated day.
scenarios.reasoning: R2: a repeated local date is one day, so the Tokyo and Honolulu entries for 2026-10-06 are evaluated once and there is one expected row for it. The streak goes 1, 2, 3 — not 4.

scenarios.description: Flying Los Angeles → Sydney crosses the date line westward and skips local Tuesday; the skipped date is not a missed day.
scenarios.reasoning: R2: 2026-10-06 never exists locally for this traveller, so it is not a miss. The streak continues from 1 to 2 with no forgiveness used.

scenarios.description: Five straight kept days fire the first aura milestone letter.
scenarios.reasoning: R3 counts five consecutive kept days, and R7 fires milestone-5 on Friday because the streak is a positive multiple of 5 on a kept day. Forgiveness is never used, so it stays available all week and the count remains 0.

scenarios.description: Fifteen straight kept days fire milestone letters at 5, 10 and 15.
scenarios.reasoning: With no misses at all, R3 climbs uninterrupted and R7 fires milestone-5, milestone-10 and milestone-15 on the exact days the streak hits those values. Both Sundays run the week-end update with no forgiven day and no break, so the count stays 0 and no week-end letter fires.

scenarios.description: Friday's forgiven miss lands exactly on streak 5, co-firing the forgive letter and the milestone letter.
scenarios.reasoning: Friday's miss is forgiven under R4, and R7 explicitly covers forgiven days, so the streak reaches 5 and both forgive-1 and milestone-5 fire, in that order. The Sunday week-end update then raises the count to 1.

scenarios.description: A second miss in the same week breaks the streak at 4, one day short of the milestone.
scenarios.reasoning: Monday's miss is forgiven but Friday's miss fails R4a (a day was already forgiven that week), so the streak resets to 0 at 4 and no milestone fires; R7 reports null because the day was neither kept nor forgiven. R5 zeroes the count immediately on the break day, and the weekend's kept days restart the streak at 1 and 2.

scenarios.description: A full week evaluated in Australia/Sydney with one forgiven miss.
scenarios.reasoning: The scenario timezone is Australia/Sydney, so R1 and R2 use Sydney local dates for day and week boundaries. Tuesday's miss is forgiven (forgive-1), Friday hits streak 5 and fires milestone-5, and the Sunday week-end update moves the count to 1.

scenarios.description: Twenty straight kept days: milestone letters fire at 5, 10 and 15, but day 20 reports the value with no letter.
scenarios.reasoning: R7 reports auraMilestone 20 on 2026-10-20 because the streak is a positive multiple of 5, but no milestone letter exists beyond milestone-15, so lettersFired is empty that day. The earlier milestones at 5, 10 and 15 each fired their letters normally.

scenarios.description: Six weeks mixing forgiven Sundays and Mondays, a clean week, a DST week, a mid-week break, and milestones with and without letters.
scenarios.reasoning: Weeks 1-2 each forgive one miss and the count reaches 2; week 3 is fully clean so its Sunday resets the count to 0 and fires forgive-restored. Week 4's Thursday miss is forgiven on streak 25, which reports auraMilestone 25 with no letter. Week 5 forgives Tuesday (forgive-2) then breaks on Thursday's second miss (streak-broken), zeroing the count immediately. Week 6 recovers: Saturday's miss is forgiven (forgive-1) and Sunday hits streak 10, firing milestone-10.

scenarios.description: After the limit break on Monday, a second miss the same week also breaks the streak (R4c: forgiveness stays off after any break until next Monday).
scenarios.reasoning: Weeks 1–3 each forgive one miss (count 1, 2, 3; warning on the third Sunday). Monday of week 4 misses with the count at 3, so R4b breaks the streak (streak-broken-after-limit) and R5 sets the count to 0. Wednesday's miss is not forgiven because the streak already broke this week (R4c), so it breaks again (streak-broken). Forgiveness is available again from the next Monday.

scenarios.description: The week's second miss lands on Sunday: the break and the week-end update happen on the same evaluation.
scenarios.reasoning: Monday's miss is forgiven (forgive-1), so Sunday's miss fails R4a and breaks the streak, firing streak-broken and zeroing the count immediately. The Sunday week-end update then sees a week with a break and keeps the count at 0; no week-end letter fires because forgive-restored requires a break-free week.

scenarios.description: One forgiven miss in week 1, then a fully clean week 2 restores forgiveness.
scenarios.reasoning: Week 1 forgives Wednesday's miss (forgive-1) and the Sunday week-end update moves the count to 1; Sunday's kept day also hits streak 5 and fires milestone-5. Week 2 has no miss and no break, so its Sunday week-end update resets the count to 0 and fires forgive-restored, proving a single clean week re-arms forgiveness.

scenarios.description: Three straight Monday forgivenesses; the third Monday co-fires forgive-3-limit with milestone-15 and the warning follows on Sunday.
scenarios.reasoning: Each Monday miss is forgiven while the count climbs 0 to 1 to 2. The third Monday lands on streak 15, so forgive-3-limit and milestone-15 co-fire in that order. The week-end update then raises the count to 3 and fires forgive-off-warning on Sunday.

scenarios.description: Week 2's forgiven day is its Sunday, firing forgive-2 on the same evaluation as the week-end update.
scenarios.reasoning: Week 1 forgives Wednesday's miss (forgive-1) and the count moves to 1; Sunday's kept day hits streak 5 and fires milestone-5. Week 2 keeps six days, so the Sunday miss lands on streak 12 and is forgiven because the count was 1, firing forgive-2. The Sunday week-end update then raises the count to 2.
